security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, when a guest CSR write to mseccfg attempts to clear the MML bit while MML=1 and the Smepmp extension is implemented, if the WARL sticky-bit logic permits the write to succeed (clearing MML to 0) without a full PMP reset, the emulation violates the normative rule that MML is a sticky bit that 'once set cannot be unset until a PMP reset'.
security_spec.summary: mseccfg.MML sticky-bit not enforced on CSR write, allowing guest to bypass Smepmp M-mode lockdown and escalate to M-mode access on S/U-mode-only PMP regions

findings.finding: Sticky-bit logic for MML and MMWP is correctly implemented. Line 688 'val |= (env->mseccfg & mask)' ORs the current MML/MMWP bits back into val, so any write attempting to clear MML from 1→0 has MML forced back to 1. Line 689-691 triggers TLB flush only when sticky bits actually change (i.e., on first transition 0→1). This correctly enforces the normative rule that 'MML once set cannot be unset until a PMP reset'.

RLB write-enable check only considers entries with explicit PMP_LOCK bit (via pmp_is_locked()). Under MML=1, PMP entries configured as Shared-Region (encodings 12-14) are implicitly locked per the Smepmp spec even without the LOCK bit. The spec requires RLB to be unwritable when ANY entry is locked (explicitly or implicitly). This allows RLB to be incorrectly set to 1 when MML=1 and implicitly-locked Shared-Region entries exist, potentially weakening PMP enforcement by making locked entries writable.

env.mseccfg is not included in any VMStateDescription (neither vmstate_riscv_cpu fields nor any subsection, including vmstate_pmp at line 60-71). If a VM is live-migrated while MML=1, the destination will receive mseccfg=0 (default/uninitialized), silently clearing the MML sticky bit across migration. This bypasses the normative rule that MML can only be cleared by PMP reset — the migration boundary acts as an unintended PMP reset without any explicit reset event.

CPU reset correctly clears mseccfg=0 and calls pmp_unlock_entries(). Per the privileged spec and Smepmp spec, a hart reset (including PMP reset) is the legitimate and only mechanism to clear the MML sticky bit. The reset path is correct and does not violate the normative rule.
